decisions.reason: This drain housing is closely related to the firm's established drainage engineering and customizable system know-how, and its own-page presence in 2018 and 2019 suggests enough market relevance to justify continued learning rather than withdrawal.

A floor-level shower drainage system sits at the center of the firm's stated strategic direction toward integrated, low-profile bathroom drainage, so its strong fit with existing knowledge makes continued commercialization very likely.

As a flagship designer shower drainage product, it is highly aligned with the firm's design-conscious drainage specialization, and the shift from a standalone page to a website mention is more consistent with portfolio integration than with an imminent exit.

The shower element with integrated slope is a natural complement to the firm's installation solutions and waterproofing guidance, so even with only modest website prominence it remains close enough to core capabilities to keep.

The backflow-protected basement floor drain builds directly on the firm's drainage technology and was prominently promoted at launch and on the home page, which supports retaining it as a technically related extension of the core business.

The air-admittance valve is somewhat less central to the firm's main shower-drainage focus, but it is still an adjacent plumbing product for the same installer audience, so a capable engineering-led firm would more likely keep it than drop it immediately.
